subject: Neurology
vignette: A woman in labor receives an analgesic that is a μ-opioid receptor partial agonist and a κ-opioid receptor full agonist. It provides good analgesia with less respiratory depression than morphine.
question: Which of the following best describes butorphanol and nalbuphine?

options.text: Pure μ agonists with high intrinsic activity and marked respiratory depression
Opioid antagonists used to reverse overdose
Mixed agonist/antagonists: μ partial agonists and κ full agonists
Peripherally acting antagonists used for constipation
Weak agonists that inhibit serotonin reuptake

explanation_correct: Butorphanol and nalbuphine are mixed agonist/antagonists: they are partial agonists at μ-opioid receptors and full agonists at κ-opioid receptors. They provide analgesia for severe pain such as labor pain and cause less respiratory depression than full opioid agonists.

explanation_incorrect.A: They are not pure μ agonists; they are partial at μ and full at κ, which limits respiratory depression.
explanation_incorrect.B: Opioid antagonists are naloxone, naltrexone, and methylnaltrexone, not butorphanol/nalbuphine.
explanation_incorrect.D: Peripherally acting antagonists for constipation describe methylnaltrexone.
explanation_incorrect.E: Serotonin reuptake inhibition with weak opioid agonism describes tramadol.

educationalObjective: Butorphanol and nalbuphine are μ partial/κ full agonists with less respiratory depression than full agonists.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient who has been taking a full opioid agonist chronically for pain is given butorphanol for additional analgesia. Shortly afterward, he develops anxiety, tremor, sweating, and abdominal cramps.
question: Which of the following best explains this reaction?

options.text: Butorphanol has higher intrinsic activity at μ receptors than the full agonist, causing toxicity
As a μ partial agonist, butorphanol competes with the full agonist and can precipitate opioid withdrawal
Butorphanol is an antagonist at κ receptors, reversing analgesia
The reaction is an allergic response mediated by histamine release
Butorphanol inhibits CYP2D6, causing accumulation of the full agonist

explanation_correct: In a patient dependent on a full μ agonist, giving a partial agonist such as butorphanol can precipitate withdrawal because the partial agonist competes for the receptor but has lower intrinsic activity, reducing overall opioid signaling. Mixed agonist/antagonists are also not easily reversed by naloxone. Their respiratory depression is less than that of full agonists.

explanation_incorrect.A: Butorphanol has lower, not higher, intrinsic activity at μ receptors than a full agonist; that is why it can precipitate withdrawal.
explanation_incorrect.C: Butorphanol is a κ full agonist, not an antagonist; κ antagonism is not the mechanism here.
explanation_incorrect.D: This is not an allergic or histaminergic reaction; it is receptor-level precipitated withdrawal.
explanation_incorrect.E: CYP2D6 inhibition is not the mechanism; codeine is the prodrug dependent on CYP2D6.

educationalObjective: Giving a μ partial agonist to a patient on a full agonist can precipitate withdrawal; mixed agonist/antagonists are not easily reversed by naloxone.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient with neuropathic pain uses a topical cream derived from hot peppers. It produces an initial burning sensation followed by prolonged pain relief. Laboratory studies show reduced release of substance P from nociceptive fibers.
question: Which of the following best describes capsaicin's mechanism of action?

options.text: Competitive antagonism at μ-opioid receptors in the CNS
Inhibition of cyclooxygenase in peripheral tissues
Excessive stimulation and desensitization of nociceptive fibers, decreasing substance P release
Blockade of voltage-gated Na+ channels on sensory axons
Agonism at GABA-B receptors in the spinal cord

explanation_correct: Capsaicin, found in hot peppers, acts by excessively stimulating and then desensitizing nociceptive fibers, leading to decreased substance P release and reduced pain. It is used topically for musculoskeletal and neuropathic pain. The initial burning sensation reflects the excitatory phase before desensitization.

explanation_incorrect.A: Opioid antagonism is not capsaicin's mechanism; naloxone/naltrexone are opioid antagonists.
explanation_incorrect.B: COX inhibition is the mechanism of NSAIDs, not capsaicin.
explanation_incorrect.D: Na+ channel blockade is the mechanism of local anesthetics, not capsaicin.
explanation_incorrect.E: GABA-B agonism in the spinal cord is the mechanism of baclofen.

educationalObjective: Capsaicin desensitizes nociceptive fibers and decreases substance P release, used for neuropathic and musculoskeletal pain.
